### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **30** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7218b8e3df2a7038d0dfac1f9406e293545435a9` — the merge of head `8d50ecd6e1b8d303cb81284d6388c0493160898a` into base `fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7218b8e3df2a7038d0dfac1f9406e293545435a9 && git checkout 7218b8e3df2a7038d0dfac1f9406e293545435a9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2 8d50ecd6e1b8d303cb81284d6388c0493160898a && git checkout -B drift-repro fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2 && git merge --no-ff 8d50ecd6e1b8d303cb81284d6388c0493160898a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## L1 review (L1-d) · 2026-11-17T20:17Z

L1: ACCEPT
Head-sha: `8d50ecd6e1b8d303cb81284d6388c0493160898a`

Read against restated claim 6957357767 (after seat Premise corrected 6957305509, which scopes this to recommendation 1), premise report 6957257121 and fix report 6958985208 on #34916.
- **Size:** 6 files, +503/-1.
- **Not governed:** `check-governed-merges --branch pr-34965` reports 0 of 6 paths and 504 lines.
- **CI at this head:** 37 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed, all concluded.
- **Claim surface:** all 6 files are inside it: the two source files, a new test beside each, the REST pin under `packages/rest/src/`, and the changeset.

### What holds
- **Closing keyword.** The card's symptom is the stored text `'true'`. This head stores the boolean, and the wider defect the premise found (a stored `'false'` read as `true`) is fixed on the read side. Both are within the seat's recommendation 1.
- **The accepted set is unchanged (`Clause-②: no` holds).**
  - `BOOLEAN_READINGS` is exactly the validator's boolean arm (`record-validator.ts:1681`: `0`, `1`, `'0'`, `'1'`, `'true'`, `'false'`), compared by SameValueZero.
  - A value outside it (`'yes'`, `'TRUE'`, `2`, an array) is left as sent for the arm to refuse with `invalid_boolean`. A CONTROL pin covers this at POST and at the batch.
  - The boolean arm `continue`s before the numeric and array branches, so no other branch sees a boolean field.
  - The pure-copy contract (same reference when nothing changed, a shallow copy otherwise) is kept and pinned.
- **One choke point.** The arm sits in `normalizeNumericStringRow`, the normalisation every insert, update and validate door reaches (the #29241/#29562 pattern). So the REST pin over SqlDriver shows all four doors (single POST/PATCH and `/batch` create/update) storing `1`/`0`. Both `won = true` and `won = false` find exactly their rows, and `requiredWhen: record.won == true` refuses `'true'` with no date on every door, just as it refuses `true`.
- **Read side.** `presentStoredBoolean` maps only the four text spellings and keeps `Boolean(value)` for everything else, so numbers and booleans read exactly as before. A legacy `'false'` row reads `false` at GET, and that is pinned.
- **Ablations.** Removing the engine arm turns 16 unit tests and 3 REST tests red. Reverting the read turns 2 unit tests and 1 REST test red. Both were restored.
- **Changeset.** It is a patch on `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/driver-sql`, and its text matches the diff. It says plainly that an equality filter on a legacy text row matches only after a re-save.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1: **`presentReadValue` stays a follow-up, not this PR.** I read `sql-driver-filter-helpers.ts:305`: `presentReadValue` has no boolean kind at all (`readPresentationKind` yields date, time, datetime, audit_timestamp and number). So `distinct()` and `aggregate()` keys over a boolean column already present the raw stored value (`1`/`0` on SQLite) for every row, not only the legacy text ones. That is a pre-existing presentation gap with its own surface (a new presentation kind across dialects, plus its own pins). This PR does not widen it, and it is outside the claim. I recommend the seat route it to triage beside the two named follow-ups.
- N2: A `beforeInsert`/`beforeUpdate` hook on a boolean field now sees `true`/`false` where it used to see the string reading. That is the intended canonical value and the same effect #29241 had for numbers. I note it only for the record.

Landing: not governed and green on this exact head. `Clause-②: no` and no contract face is touched, so area o3-A lands it. A later push owes a delta read.
